questions.prompt: Automated fraction 0.90 and rubric 13 points out of 16 (four criteria). Milestone score.
Which condition is NOT part of the graduation rule?
options: The learner must have built the optional hardware tier, since graduation always includes a real robot.
Every gate check of every milestone passes.
Every milestone scores at least 60 and the total at least 70.
CAP08 reports zero safety violations and reproduce-smoke passes on a clean checkout.
questions.explanation: The hardware tier is optional and never required (nor can it replace a failing gate).

questions.prompt: Total 88 with a Nav2 baseline stretch completed and all gates passed. Grade?
options: Distinction, because a stretch is done.
Pass, because Merit needs two completed stretches and a higher total.
Merit: total is 80 to 89.
Not graduated, because stretches must be hardware.
questions.explanation: Distinction needs total >= 90 and a stretch.

questions.prompt: Why does the smoke test compare outcomes (success, cause, steps) rather than raw floating-point values?
options: Floating-point values are never reproducible, not even on one single machine.
Tiny differences between CPUs are expected; the outcome should not change.
Raw values are too large to store in JSON.
Outcomes are easier to fake.
questions.explanation: Compare what matters and what is stable; document the tolerance for continuous values.

questions.prompt: Maximum total time in minutes allowed for the reproduce-smoke run.

options: FROM python:latest and pip install at container start.
Download the model weights from a URL when the container runs.
Use a floating base tag so that the image receives security updates automatically.
Pinned base, lock file at build, network off.
questions.explanation: Everything needed at run time should be inside the image with exact versions.

questions.prompt: Wilson lower bound 0.7014 rendered with the pct1 format: the number before the percent sign.
A Results sentence reads 'success was 78.3 %' typed by hand. Which test catches it?
options: The ruff lint check that runs over the whole repository.
A scan of Results for bare numbers.
The git tag check.
The Docker build.
questions.explanation: The template scan flags bare numbers in Results.

questions.prompt: The limitations section should say, at minimum, which of these?
options: Simulation only; twin is not reality; no certified safety.
The code has no bugs left.
The robot works in every environment we could imagine testing.
Limitations are optional if the results are good.
questions.explanation: State scope and what was not tested.

questions.prompt: Maximum number of commands in the README quickstart.
When may a box in RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md be ticked?
options: When you intend to do it well before the final deadline arrives.
When a teammate says it is probably fine.
After you verified it on a clean checkout.
At the end, all at once, to save time.
questions.explanation: Ticking without verifying defeats the checklist.

questions.prompt: Plan a 3-minute demo video: which shots, which overlays and what must be shown honestly?
rubric: Typed instruction through completed task, with parse result visible.
Overlay of estimator pose and detections, and the safety supervisor state, including one safety stop.
Time allocation that sums to 180 s with a closing slide of metrics and limitations.
Shows or mentions a failure case and states that it is simulation only.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Write a test plan for report/render.py covering unknown keys, unknown formats, unresolved placeholders and number formatting.
rubric: Unknown metric path raises KeyError naming the path.
Unknown format and non-numeric targets (dict, list, bool, None) raise errors.
Output never contains '{{' and a template without placeholders is unchanged.
Formatting checked on known values (for example 0.7014 with pct1 gives 70.1 %) plus a mutation check on metrics.json.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
